text:
Mei: Quick hit this morning: P99 bursts traced to synchronous host handoff + repeated demote/promote churn. Repro attached.
Carlos: Minimal trace?
Mei:
```
[2026-03-23T08:11:10Z] req=0x2f stage=ENCODE
[2026-03-23T08:11:10Z] kv: demote tenant=gamma
[2026-03-23T08:11:10Z] pool: host_acquire blocking -> 85ms
[2026-03-23T08:11:10Z] resume
```
Jonah: 85ms is consistent with host page-in + NVMe stall. We should avoid blocking the hot inference thread.
Priya: Proposed incremental plan: 1) add demote_cooldown_ms (default 500ms) to reduce thrash, 2) non-blocking acquire that returns {ok,pending,fail}, 3) small Lease GC with per-tenant pending_bytes cap and auto-cancel after 20s.
Mei: I like that. Also add lease_pending_bytes metric and lease_gc_count. Alert if pending > 70% cap.
Carlos: Edge case: pending lease reads. Our options: return cache-miss (recompute), serve stale shadow, or block. Default to recompute for correctness. Document options in RFC.
Jonah: For POC I'll wire non-blocking acquire + recompute-on-pending. We'll gate via config offload.acquire_mode.
Priya: I'll run canary with demote_cooldown=500 and offload.acquire_mode=nonblocking. Ops: infra-bot, deploy canary tag=lease-cooldown-2026-03-23
infra-bot: deploy requested tag=lease-cooldown-2026-03-23
infra-bot: deploy completed on 4/4 canaries
Mei: Canary results: P99 down 45%, but host memory climbed on node-3 -> triggered OOM mitigation. Looks like our pending cap too high.
Carlos: Lower per-node pending cap to 40MB and add early fail into fallback routing.
Jonah: I'll add a small offload-queue length metric and a unit test simulating slow host alloc. PR incoming.
Priya: I'll update dashboard and add alert for lease_pending_bytes > 80% of cap and fallback_triggered>0.
Mei: Follow-ups: Jonah RFC for Lease lifecycle (ownership, cancel, recovery), Ops to tune caps, and Carlos to implement early-fail fallback. We'll reconvene after next canary.
